title: Priv: Isolated network & offline patching requirements for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Rao
description: PRD: Define minimal networking, upgrade/patch, and offline-operations requirements and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC (customer-managed) deployments that operate with restricted or no egress to the public Internet. Goal is to enable supportable install, patching, and rollback flows for customers operating in isolated or regulated networks while minimizing Redwood-managed external dependencies.
requirements: Networking: Support deployments with zero direct outbound egress to public Internet. Customers may provide a bastion/proxy/NAT or run entirely NATless; Redwood must document supported patterns and compatibility constraints.

Networking: All external artifact retrieval (images, packages, model bundles) must be possible via a customer-hosted artifact registry (OCI registry, private Docker registry, or internal package mirror). Redwood will provide manifest lists and signed metadata for offline mirror seeding.
Networking: DNS: allow configuration of customer-supplied DNS servers; where DNS is restricted, allow images and artifact manifests to use IPs or pre-seeded hosts file approach documented by Redwood.
Networking: Time sync: support customers who cannot reach public NTP — document local NTP/hardware RTC expectations for certificate validity checks and signed artifact verification.

Networking: Optional HTTP/HTTPS proxy support with basic auth and TLS interception guidance. The installer and health-check tooling must honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY environment variables.

Artifact security: All downloadable artifacts (images, tarballs, model weights, runtime binaries) must be signed by Redwood and accompanied by an SBOM and SHA-256 checksum. Customers must be able to validate signatures offline using a provided Redwood public key bundle.

Installer/Updater: Provide an offline installer bundle (tarball) that contains runtime images, Helm charts, CRDs, and migration scripts. The bundle must be ingestible into an internal registry without internet access.

Upgrade orchestration: Support upgrade orchestration that can run entirely on-cluster without outbound calls. Provide a CLI/controller mode that performs staged upgrades, can respect a maintenance window, and can pause/abort on health-check failures.
Rollback: Any automated upgrade flow must include documented and tested rollback steps that restore model-serving state (KV caches, model versions) or fail safely to a pinned model version.

Observability: Telemetry and logs: default behavior must not send telemetry offsite. Provide explicit opt-in remote telemetry toggles; otherwise all logs remain in-cluster or to customer-specified logging endpoints.
Credentials/KMS: Allow integration with customer-managed KMS/HSM endpoints that are reachable privately. Securely support keys via sealed secrets or PV-based key files for air-gapped installs.
Maintenance window API: Expose an API/CLI to schedule maintenance windows during which automatic rollouts/scale-downs can run. Maintenance windows must be honored by the upgrade controller.

Compatibility: Document supported Kubernetes distributions, minimum OS/kernel requirements, and required CNI behaviors (e.g., whether hostPort usage or nodePort is allowed). Identify unsupported combos up front.
Compliance artifacts: Provide a signed manifest for each release with release notes, CVE summaries, and SHA checksums suitable for internal audit and packaging into customer compliance bundles.

Performance: Binaries and model artifacts must be downloadable and loadable without external model resolution; runtime must be able to serve from local model cache on first startup if the registry is pre-seeded.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A customer can perform a fresh install in a VPC with no outbound internet (egress blocked) using only a pre-seeded internal OCI registry and a provided offline installer bundle. Installation completes without Redwood-managed outbound dependencies.

AC-2: Upgrade flow can be executed entirely within the customer environment: operator runs 'redwood upgrade --bundle <path>' and the controller performs a staged rollout across nodes honoring a configurable maintenance window. Upgrade can be paused and resumed.

AC-3: All artifacts consumed during install/upgrade are accompanied by SHA-256 checksums and detached signatures; the installer verifies signatures against a shipped public key before applying changes. Verification failures abort the operation with clear exit codes and logs.

AC-4: Rollback test: simulate a failing post-upgrade health-check and confirm the controller can automatically revert to the previous pinned runtime and model set within a documented timeout. The test must preserve data PVs and model cache consistency.

AC-5: No telemetry or usage payloads are sent outside the customer's network by default. Enabling remote telemetry requires explicit operator action and documented steps that include legal/consent language.
AC-6: CLI and controller honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY environment variables during all artifact pulls. Tests must run with a proxy endpoint and validate connectivity.
AC-7: Signed SBOM and release manifest are available in the offline bundle. Auditors can reconcile installed binary checksums against the release manifest offline.

AC-8: Public-key rotation: customers can replace the Redwood public verification keys used by the installer with their own trust store; the installer should support '--trusted-keys <file>' and validate accordingly.

AC-9: Documented procedures and runbooks for emergency patching (apply hotfix image, roll nodes) exist in Confluence and a runbook playbook (step list) is included with release notes. A sample GitHub PR and example manifests are linked.

AC-10: Support matrix: a clear compatibility table for supported Kubernetes versions, container runtimes, and CNI plugins is published and linked from the installer. Installer will fail fast with a readable error message if an unsupported environment is detected.
AC-11: Time-sync constraint tests: installer warns if system clock skew exceeds allowed threshold and provides remediation steps for local NTP or manual clock set.
notes:
Progress & implementation guidance:
- 2026-03-02: Requirements draft reviewed with Security and Infra; they requested SBOM + signature verification and explicit no-telemetry-by-default behavior.
- 2026-03-05: Engineering proposed an 'offline bundle' artifact format (tar.gz of images + manifest + signatures).
- 2026-03-09: Design to provide UX text for maintenance window scheduling and CLI UX.
- Open questions: how to handle large model weight distribution for customers without internal image registries (proposal to support direct upload via S3-compatible endpoints during install).
decisions: Use detached PGP-style signatures for artifact verification in the first GA to avoid complex HSM key distribution requirements.
Default: telemetry disabled. Offering an opt-in agent that can forward telemetry to Redwood for customers who choose it.
Provide both a CLI-only offline install path and a controller-assisted upgrade path to support different ops preferences.
next_steps: ENG: Implement offline bundle generator and signature tooling (ENG-4021).
DOCS: Draft offline-install runbook and checklist for auditors; include SBOM verification steps.
SEC: Validate signature format and key rotation approach; sign-off target 2026-03-20.
PM: Coordinate early adopter with infra team for a zero-egress install test (target 2026-03-30).
